justification: B opens on a full cover and holds one banded system through the pages, with the panel set into the picture. A has a small masthead instead of a cover and ends with a half-used page, though its large headings read well.

A keeps the story moving over three full pages with a pull quote and a big picture. B leaves a last page holding one heading and two lines, and its chart page breaks awkwardly. A's dark panel at the top of page 3 is small and a little stray.
The two are the same pages but for a filled against a ruled figure strip and a footer band. Neither changes how the report reads.
B holds the statements in two full pages under clear bands and gives the chart real size. A has larger, calmer type but its third page is half empty and the chart small.

B sets the two languages side by side, pairs the charts and puts each statement in a compact ledger with its title on top. A stacks the languages and splits a table over a page. B's last page is thin, with a lone panel.

A is orderly: banded headings, a composed cover and every section starting cleanly. B has the stronger cover picture but strands a section heading at the foot of page 2, away from its text. A leaves more white at the foot of its pages.
The same pages to the eye: same bands, pictures and tables, with only a slight change to the figures strip on page 1.

B gives the paper a cover, serif text at a reading size and room around its tables. A packs the whole paper into two tight pages of small type, which is efficient but tiring. B's pages run half empty and it is much longer.
Same pages, but A tints the current period in each table, which helps a reader find the figure that matters. The difference is small.

B has a real cover and a calmer rule system. A has no cover and a whole page of two charts, though its banded headings are clear. B leaves a section heading near the foot of page 3 with only two lines under it.
Same pages. B's filled head and foot bands give a manual firmer page furniture than A's thin lines, at no cost to the text.

A sets the languages side by side and lays the panel over the picture. B stacks them and separates the year's figures from their heading across the page turn. A's last page is half used and starts with a stray line.
The two papers look the same on both pages.

B holds the statements in three firm pages with a filled figures strip and banded headings, which suits the document. A has a cover and more air, but several pages run half empty. Both end on a thin last page.

A gives the report a cover, a hero figure and a chapter strip, so the pages change pace. B is the same content in four tight banded pages, and its last page holds one small table. A runs long and its text pages are loose.
Same pages. A's filled head and foot bands give a manual firmer page furniture than B's thin lines.
Same pages, with B tinting one column of each table, which gives the eye a place to land. The difference is small. The chart title looks soft in both.
Same pages but for a ruled against a filled figures strip on page 1; each suits the page equally.

A opens on a full picture with the title below it and sets pictures across the column, so it reads as an edited annual report. B has a plain logo cover and centred pictures, and looks like a default report, though nothing in it is wrong.
A lays the same dark panel over two pictures, hiding them and repeating itself. B lets the first picture run the full width and keeps text beside the others. B's last page opens with a stray line.
A sets both languages side by side and joins picture and text in one panel, filling two pages evenly. B stacks them and leaves the year's figures at the top of page 2, away from their heading.

B holds together over six pages with a picture cover and panels in the pictures. A is elegant and has a hero figure, but its contents page and letter page are mostly white and it runs to eight pages. B's last page is thin.

B has a picture cover, sets the languages side by side, titles the table above its heads and pairs the two charts small. A stacks the languages, spends a page on two large charts and has a thin logo cover.
B is composed over four pages. A has the bolder cover title but its panel floats alone at the top of page 4 and its last page holds two lines.

B has a clean cover and sets text inside the pictures, with even pages. A has a masthead and its picture cuts a paragraph, leaving a lone line under the image. A's large picture is strong, but the reading breaks.
B has a cover and serif type with well-spaced statements, and ends on a full page. A is tight and banded and leaves a last page with one small table.
The two papers look the same on both pages.

B is orderly: banded headings and tinted tables over full pages. A has the bigger pictures, but a section heading sits with two lines at the foot of page 4 and its last page is thin. B's cover title wraps awkwardly in its column.
The same pages to the eye, apart from a slight change to the figures strip on page 1.
A has a clean cover and even pages with panels set in the pictures. B has a masthead in place of a cover and tighter, less settled pages.

A holds the data in rows of small charts over four composed pages. B has elegant type, a hero figure and chapter openers but spreads thin content over eight pages, with two openers nearly empty. A's last page is thin.
Nearly the same design. A skips the contents page and the number marks, and a six-page report does not need them; B is a page longer for no gain.
B spreads the proposal evenly over three pages under large headings. A's last page holds only the team note, under a band, leaving most of the page white.
B runs the quay picture across the page and keeps the other beside its text. A puts the same dark panel over both pictures, hiding much of each. The rest of the two reports match.
B fits the brief on two pages under clear bands. A sets the recommendation alone on a third page with two lines on it, which weakens the point the paper exists to make. A has the calmer serif type.

A has a picture cover, sets the languages side by side, titles the table above its heads and pairs the two charts small. B stacks the languages, spends a page on two large charts and has a thin logo cover.
A's banded pages hold a picture and text panel and read as designed. B has a thin logo cover, a page with one chart and a very tall picture. A's last page holds only two lines.
A runs the quay picture across the page and keeps the other beside its text. B puts the same dark panel over both pictures, hiding much of each. The rest of the two reports match.

A joins pictures and short text in green panels with a banded title. B gives each section its own page and a large centred picture under a logo cover, which is clear but repetitive and more white than needed.
B has a filled cover, a hero figure, charts grouped in rows and a chapter opener. A has a thin logo cover and one large chart after another over eight pages, and a table strands at the top of page 7.
A holds the story over six fuller pages with strong headings. B is longer, and its opener pages hold only a few lines, though its colour is warmer and its rhythm more varied.
Same pages but for a ruled against a filled figures strip and a changed foot band. Neither reads better.
B sets the two languages side by side and joins the picture and text in a panel, so page 2 has one clear event. A stacks the languages and its picture is small, with looser text.
A has a filled cover, a hero figure, charts grouped in rows and a chapter opener. B has a thin logo cover and one large chart after another over eight pages, and a table strands at the top of page 7.
The same structure. A has calmer serif headings and B firmer page bands and numbering; neither is clearly better.
Same pages but for a ruled against a filled figures strip and a footer band; neither changes how the report reads.
A gives the manual a cover and an even serif page with air around the steps. B has a masthead and wide heavy headings set against narrow text, which feels less settled for a manual.
The two briefs look the same on both pages, but for a slightly firmer table rule in B.

A sets the languages side by side, pairs the charts and puts each statement in a compact ledger with its title on top. B stacks the languages and splits a table over a page. A's last page is thin, with a lone panel.
Same pages, but B tints the current period in each table, which helps a reader find the figure that matters. The difference is small.

B holds one banded system over three pages with text set beneath its picture. A's heavy heads compete with the narrow text, its last page starts on stray lines and half the page is empty. A's large picture is strong.
The two briefs look the same on both pages.
The same structure. A has firmer page bands and numbering and B calmer serif headings; neither is clearly better.

B keeps text whole, with the short passages set inside the pictures. In A the large picture cuts a paragraph and leaves a lone line under it, and a sentence runs on to the top of page 3. A's picture has more impact.
A is composed over four pages. B has the bolder cover title but its panel floats alone at the top of page 4 and its last page holds two lines.
B balances the paper over two even pages at a good reading size. A crams nearly everything on page 1 and leaves a page with a stray bullet and a few lines.
B runs the picture across the page and keeps the text in the column, so the picture is seen whole. A lays a dark panel over most of it. Otherwise the two match.
Same pages but for a filled against a ruled figures strip on page 1; each suits the page equally.
B's serif headings with coloured rules look more considered for a board paper than A's plain numbered headings. Content and spacing are otherwise the same.
B sets its title on the cover picture, keeps the pictures clear and has larger text under a steady top band. A lays dark panels over its pictures and its body text is small and grey.
A has a full cover and calm serif heads aligned with the text. B's heavy heads hang out to the left of a narrow column, which feels unsettled for a manual.

A keeps one colour through heads, band and chart, though its first page is half empty. B fills page 1 better but its black chart and black heads do not belong with the red masthead, and its second page is half empty.
A shows its pictures whole, one of them across the page. B covers two pictures with dark panels. A's pull line sits alone at the foot of page 3, a small fault.
A sets the languages side by side and uses a picture with a panel to fill page 2. B stacks the languages, has a small picture and leaves the foot of page 2 empty.
A leads with a big figure, sets the charts as small multiples and opens a section with a designed page. B runs one large chart after another over eight plain pages.
A fills two balanced pages. B has larger type and a stronger masthead, but its first page is half empty and its last holds a chart and a note.
A holds a coherent banded journal page over two pages. B's heavy heads hang outside the column, its black chart clashes with the red masthead and a table runs on to the next page.
A has a picture cover, generous serif pages and a figures row, though page 4 leaves a gap under its picture. B is packed small and ends on a page holding a single table.
A keeps paragraphs whole with the short passages inside the pictures. In B the large picture cuts a paragraph and text runs on to the tops of pages 2 and 3, though the picture itself is striking.
A shows its picture clear across the page, while B covers much of it with a dark panel. The rest of the two proposals match.

A has a picture cover, languages side by side, paired charts and ledgers. B is plainer and stacks the languages, with a very large chart alone at the top of page 4. A leaves white beside its narrow columns on page 2.
Same pages, but A tints the key column of each table, which helps the eye a little.
